evals.name: diff-default-read-only
evals.prompt: Review the animations in my current changes before I open the PR.
evals.expected_output: The skill reviews only the animation in the working diff, edits nothing and says so, runs the write-css review pre-pass on changed CSS-styled files, and reports each finding with a severity, a file:line, the catalog rule it breaks, and whether it is verified from code or needs a device recording.
expectations: No file is edited, and the answer says the review is read-only
Findings are limited to animation in the changed files
Each finding carries a severity and a file:line
Each finding is labeled verified from code or needs a device recording
evals.source: the skill's default diff mode, written for this suite

evals.name: tree-audit-offers-handoff
evals.prompt: Audit every animation in this codebase.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs tree mode over the whole repository, groups findings by severity, edits nothing, and with many findings offers a handoff to an implementation skill instead of fixing them itself.
expectations: The audit covers the whole repository, not only the diff
Findings are grouped or ordered by severity
No file is edited
With many findings, the answer offers a handoff for the fixes instead of applying them
evals.source: the skill's tree mode, written for this suite

evals.name: opportunities-include-where-not-to-animate
evals.prompt: Where in this app would animation actually help? Don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs opportunities mode: each suggestion names the element, the purpose from the catalog and the frequency tier, and the answer also names places that should stay still (keyboard-driven or many-times-an-hour actions, data being read).
expectations: Each suggestion names a purpose (feedback, spatial consistency, state indication, preventing a jarring change, explanation or delight)
At least one place is named where animation should not be added, with the reason
No file is edited
evals.why_hard: Asked where animation helps, the model's pull is to propose motion everywhere; the catalog's frequency gate requires naming where it must not go
evals.source: reference/animation/catalog.md should-it-animate, written for this suite

evals.name: performance-cause-before-fix
evals.prompt: The sidebar animation stutters when I open it. Find out why.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs performance mode: it lists what animates and with which properties, names a cause from performance.md's diagnosis order before proposing any change, gives the swap down a tier, and labels the finding verified from code or needing a device recording.
expectations: The answer names a specific cause (for example a layout property, a busy main thread, a per-frame render or an inherited value) before proposing a change
The proposed change swaps to a cheaper property or driver rather than only adding a layer-promotion hint
The finding is labeled verified from code or needs a device recording
No file is edited
evals.why_hard: Adding a layer-promotion hint looks like a fix and is the common reflex; the case needs the cause named first
evals.source: reference/animation/performance.md diagnose, written for this suite

evals.name: fix-one-at-a-time-with-consent
evals.prompt: Review the animations in my changes and fix what you find, with --fix.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the findings, then for one finding at a time shows the exact diff and asks for a yes before applying it, never applying several unasked.
expectations: The answer shows the exact change for a finding before applying it
The answer asks for confirmation before applying a change
Changes are proposed one finding at a time
evals.source: the skill's --fix contract, written for this suite

evals.name: configured-role-duration-not-flagged
evals.prompt: Review the toast animation in src/toast.css. Our team config sets animation.duration_ms.large to 600 and the toast's transition is 400ms.
evals.expected_output: The skill judges the 400ms toast against the configured role rather than a fixed limit: a toast is within large, so the duration is not reported as a finding (or is listed as suppressed with the configured role as the reason).
expectations: The 400ms toast duration is not reported as a duration finding
The answer refers to the configured role duration, not a fixed 300ms cap
evals.why_hard: The bundled linter flags durations over its own fixed limit, so the model must overrule a tool finding with the resolved config
evals.source: the skill's duration filter, written for this suite
